title: Examples / Misuse — Prominence and signatures

location.series: IBM Logo Guidelines for Strategic Partners / Version 1.2 / copyright 2023

slide_intent: Identify hierarchy errors that change the apparent sender so readers do not attribute partner messages to IBM.
strategic_value: Consistent sender cues can keep the IBM relationship clear across documents, social posts and email.
demonstration: Red-crossed collateral, social and email examples show excessive IBM prominence, IBM social sign-off and a conflicting IBM header/partner footer.
practical_value: Inspect both the first and last brand cues in a layout, not only the presence of the right logos.

content_islands.name: Collateral prominence
content_islands.spec: Place the two-page comparison at upper left, crossing out the oversized IBM presence.

content_islands.name: Social signature
content_islands.spec: Place the social-post schematic below with IBM as the rejected sign-off.

content_islands.name: Email source confusion
content_islands.spec: Place the tall email example at right with IBM in its header and the partner at its end.

reference_purposes.Intent: The email caption explicitly explains avoiding confusion over the source of the message.
reference_purposes.Constraint: The page prohibits IBM social sign-offs, greater IBM prominence than the partner and an IBM-header/partner-signature email arrangement.
